alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain and metabolic deterioration
alerts.message: Guidelines require glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year when transitioning to DTG. This patient has gained 17 kg over 18 months on TLD, with BMI rising from 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m². She has developed pre-diabetes (fasting glucose 118 mg/dL, HbA1c 6.1%), dyslipidemia (LDL 148, triglycerides 212, HDL 38), hypertension (BP 138/88 vs baseline 118/74), and acanthosis nigricans. DTG is strongly associated with significant weight gain, which can precipitate insulin resistance. Family history of type 2 diabetes further compounds this risk. No alternative non-drug explanation accounts for the magnitude and tempo of weight gain. Virologic suppression is excellent.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for DTG-related metabolic syndrome. Consider dietary intervention, structured exercise program, and evaluate whether regimen switch away from DTG is warranted given pre-diabetes trajectory and cardiovascular risk.

alerts.title: Missing glucose monitoring plan for DTG patient
alerts.message: Guidelines specify glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year after transition to DTG. This patient transitioned to DTG 18 months ago, yet today's fasting glucose (118 mg/dL) and HbA1c (6.1%) are the first documented glycemic assessments since the switch. Baseline fasting glucose was 92 mg/dL, confirming significant deterioration. No clinician plan was documented today, so no follow-up glucose monitoring is arranged despite pre-diabetic results.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a glucose monitoring schedule. Repeat HbA1c in 3 months. Given pre-diabetes, initiate lifestyle counseling and consider metformin referral per diabetes guidelines.
